messages:

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — define success criteria and acceptance tests

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at NovusCare is aligned on doing a short evaluation next month. Before we lock dates we want a compact checklist that defines how we’ll decide success (so our procurement and risk folks can sign off). Can you send a MAP-oriented checklist that lists: acceptance tests we’ll run, exit gates (pass/fail), timelines for each activity, and any artifacts you need from us?

High level constraints:
- 4-week evaluation window (pilot environment)
- PHI-free test corpus for accuracy runs; we’ll provide sample anon datasets
- Security checklist must be completed before agents get access

If you can get something by EOD Tue (our regional team meeting), that would help us move forward.

Appreciate it,
Alex

alex.morgan@novuscare.com

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novuscare.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — define success criteria and acceptance tests

Alex — thanks, and totally agree that a compact, operational checklist is the best next step. I’ve sketched a 4-week MAP with clear pass/fail rubrics and the acceptance tests we recommend. Attaching the checklist spreadsheet (MAP-Proposed-Checklist-v1.xlsx) and linking the shared MAP doc.

Summary (quick view):
1) Week 0 — Prep & Security gating (must pass to proceed):
   - Action: NovusCare provides anonymized sample dataset + IP allowlist
   - Acceptance: KMS key exchange or temporary API-token exchange completed; security questionnaire complete
   - Exit gate: If security gaps remain after 5 business days -> pause; remediation plan required

2) Week 1 — Integration smoke tests (connectivity + inference sanity):
   - Tests: API connectivity, auth validation, streaming behavior, baseline latency (<150ms p50), basic prompt fidelity checks on 100 sample prompts
   - Exit gate (fail): If >15% prompts return unacceptable hallucination rate or latency SLO breached -> remediation sprint

3) Week 2 — Quality & edge-case validation (concordance checks):
   - Tests: 1k-run concordance test, top-K reranking QA, safety filters verified on 200 edge prompts
   - Acceptance: F1/concordance > 0.82 on labeled set; false positive safety triggers < 1%

4) Week 3 — Throughput & cost profiling (economics):
   - Tests: sustained throughput run hitting target QPS for 1 hour; cost-per-1000-tokens estimate under agreed threshold
   - Acceptance: 95th percentile latency under 300ms for production-sized batches; cost delta within ±20% forecast

5) Week 4 — Final signoff & runbook handoff:
   - Artifacts: deployment manifest, monitoring dashboards, regression test set, runbook for rollback
   - Final decision: Pass = all must-pass gates green or documented compensated mitigations accepted; Fail = critical gate unresolved

Open questions we flagged for NovusCare:
- Exact QPS target for throughput run (can you confirm?)
- Data retention policy expectations for cached prefixes

Next steps: I’ll upload the MAP doc to the shared Drive. Ben — can you review the acceptance thresholds (latency, concordance) and suggest if we should tighten for our Dedicated offering? Marissa — please include the SRE runbook stub.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novuscare.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — define success criteria and acceptance tests

Lauren / Alex — fast review from infra perspective. I like the structure. A couple of pragmatic adjustments I recommend so we don’t set unrealistic expectations during the 4-week window:

1) Latency targets: set p50 target at <120ms and p95 at <380ms for the pilot (we can aim for tighter in Dedicated PO). For the Week 1 smoke, relax p50 to <150ms as a pass-for-proceed condition.

2) Concordance & labeling: if you don’t already have 1k labeled items, we can run an initial 200-label seed with a follow-up 1k synthetic augmentation. Pass/fail should be staged: Stage A (seed): concordance >0.78, Stage B (full): >0.82.

3) Failure remediation cadence: anything falling into "remediation sprint" gets a 5-business-day fix window; if unresolved, we propose a joint risk review (exec sync).

4) Attachments: I added a short SRE runbook and a lightweight acceptance-test harness in the spreadsheet.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

- QPS target: baseline 30 QPS sustained, spike to 60 QPS for burst testing.
- We’ll provide the 200 labeled seed by Monday, and confirm timing for the larger set.
- Attached: completed security questionnaire (NovusCare_Security_Questionnaire.pdf) and a short network allowlist.

We’re happy to start Week 0 next Wednesday (18 Nov). Please confirm a short 30-min kickoff and share any credentials/workspace access we need to create.

Appreciate the thorough breakdown — looking forward to the MAP.

Alex
